To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the supramolecular aggregation process of diimidazolyl-functionalized perylenes is driven by hydrogen bonding, which is supported by π-π interactions, and that the resulting aggregates are elongated.
three diimidazolum-functionalized peryle bisimide salts aggregate into elongated supramolecular structures in chloroform, which are stabilized by π-π-stacking and hydrogen bonding.

the aggregation behavior of diimidazolim-functionalized perylenediimides in different solvents was investigated, and the results were explained with the help of DLS, SEM images, and spectroscopic data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the aggregation of three perylene bisimidazolium salts.
the aggregation processes of perylene bisimidazole derivatives in various solvents and the influence of the alkyl chain lengths.
the aggregation of perylene diimidazol salts and the formation of supramolecular assemblies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the perylene bisimidazolium salts form aggregates, which are stabilized by hydrogen bonding and π-stacking interactions.

the aggregation process of diimidazolyl perylene bisimidazolium salts is a thermodynamically controlled process, driven by the formation of hydrogen bonds and π-π stacking, leading to supramolecular assemblies.
the aggregation of the salts in solution is driven by a combination of π-π stacking, hydrogen bonding, and van der Waals forces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the supramolecular aggregation processes of the three salts studied here, are governed by the same driving forces and the same aggregation mechanism, although the length of the alkyl chain has an impact on the aggregation behavior.

the aggregation behavior of the perylene bisimidazole salts depends strongly on the alkyl chain lengths, and the aggregation behavior of perylene bis imidazolium salts is similar to the aggregation behavior of imidazolyl perylenediimides.

the aggregation of the salts in the three solvents is governed by π-π interactions, and hydrogen bonding is only relevant in glycerol, while the aggregation in chloroform is driven by enthalpy and entropy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the alkyl chain of the perylene bisimidazolium salt plays a crucial role in the aggregation process.
the aggregation of these salts is mainly controlled by the alkyl chains and the solvent, while the perylene moiety has a negligible impact on the aggregation.
the aggregation behavior of these salts can be tuned by the length of the alkyl chains.
